startupGuide.title: User Guide
startupGuide.subtitle: VocalSync can start from only the original song, or from a backing track plus the original vocal. Use UVR5 for source separation; VocalSync focuses on recording, pitch curves, guide vocal, and export.
startupGuide.step1.title: Get the original song or backing track
startupGuide.step1.body: The original song is useful for creating vocals.wav and instrumental.wav. The backing track is what you actually sing along with while recording, such as an off-vocal, karaoke version, YouTube audio, or any version with comfortable timing and key.
startupGuide.step2.title: Choose a practice flow
startupGuide.step2.body: A. Only original song: separate it in UVR5 into instrumental.wav and vocals.wav, sing with the separated instrumental, and use the separated vocal for the pitch curve and guide vocal. B. Already have a backing track: sing with your preferred backing track, then use UVR5 to extract vocals.wav from the original song.
startupGuide.step3.title: Prepare vocals with UVR5
startupGuide.step3.body: After UVR5 creates vocals.wav and instrumental.wav, return to VocalSync, import the practice backing first, then import vocals.wav as the pitch curve source. If you use another backing version, keep that backing and import only vocals.wav.
startupGuide.step4.title: Create the pitch curve and guide vocal
startupGuide.step4.body: vocals.wav is analyzed into the pitch curve. The Recording page shows the reference melody as the blue line. Guide vocal is headphone monitoring only and will not be mixed into exported vocal / mix files.
startupGuide.step5.title: Calibrate, record, and export
startupGuide.step5.body: On first use, run latency calibration so your recording aligns with the backing timeline. Before recording, check headphones, microphone, and volume levels. After recording, play back the take, then export vocal-only WAV or mix WAV.
startupGuide.tip.title: UVR5 tips
startupGuide.tip.body: For a quick check, start with a common MDX/UVR model in UVR5. For a cleaner vocal reference, run a second separation pass in UVR5, then import the final vocals.wav into VocalSync.
startupGuide.showAgain: Show this guide on next launch
uvrGuide.entry.title: What is UVR5?
uvrGuide.entry.body: UVR5 is a common vocal / instrumental separation tool. Use it to split the original song into vocals.wav and instrumental.wav, then return to VocalSync for pitch curves, guide vocal, and recording.
uvrGuide.title: UVR5 Guide
uvrGuide.subtitle: A beginner-friendly flow: create vocals.wav and instrumental.wav in UVR5, then bring those files back into VocalSync.
uvrGuide.safeDownload.title: Safe download recommendation
uvrGuide.safeDownload.body: Use the official GitHub Releases page and choose the Windows Main Download Link provided there. Avoid reuploaded, repacked, or unknown archives.
uvrGuide.step1.title: Download and open UVR5
uvrGuide.step1.body: Open the official GitHub Releases page, find the latest version, then download the Windows installer or archive. Install or extract it, then launch Ultimate Vocal Remover GUI.
uvrGuide.step2.title: Import the original song
uvrGuide.step2.body: Choose the original song you want to separate in UVR5. WAV, MP3, M4A, or audio extracted from video can work. Cleaner source audio usually gives cleaner separation.
uvrGuide.step3.title: Choose a Vocal / Instrumental model
uvrGuide.step3.body: Pick a model that outputs Vocals and Instrumental. For a first pass, try a common MDX / VR Vocal-Instrumental model, then experiment with your own second-pass workflow.
uvrGuide.step4.title: Export vocals.wav and instrumental.wav
uvrGuide.step4.body: Start separation and wait for it to finish. In the UVR5 output folder, find vocals.wav and instrumental.wav. Use vocals.wav for VocalSync pitch curves and guide vocal; use instrumental.wav as a practice backing if you like it.
uvrGuide.step5.title: Return to VocalSync and import the backing
uvrGuide.step5.body: In VocalSync's Song And Pitch Source section, import the backing you will sing to. It can be UVR5's instrumental.wav, or another off-vocal / karaoke version you prefer.
uvrGuide.step6.title: Import vocals.wav for pitch curve and guide vocal
uvrGuide.step6.body: Import vocals.wav next. VocalSync analyzes the vocal melody, draws the blue pitch curve, and uses the same vocals.wav as the headphone-only guide vocal.
uvrGuide.faq.title: FAQ
uvrGuide.faq.output.title: I cannot find the output files
uvrGuide.faq.output.body: Check UVR5's output folder setting. File names may include the original song name, model name, or Vocals / Instrumental suffix.
uvrGuide.faq.slow.title: Separation is slow
uvrGuide.faq.slow.body: GPU mode is usually faster; CPU mode has wider compatibility. Long files, video audio, and higher-quality models all increase processing time.
uvrGuide.faq.noise.title: The vocal has noise
uvrGuide.faq.noise.body: Try another model, use a cleaner source, or run a second pass with a vocal-cleaning model in UVR5. VocalSync mainly needs a clear melody reference, not release-ready dry vocals.
uvrGuide.faq.sync.title: Backing and vocals are not aligned
uvrGuide.faq.sync.body: The easiest path is using instrumental.wav and vocals.wav from the same original song. When using a different backing version, VocalSync can auto-align and you can fine-tune manually.

setup.separation.external.step1.body: Drop the original song into UVR5 and export vocals.wav plus instrumental.wav. For cleaner vocals, run a second separation pass inside UVR5.
setup.separation.external.step2.title: Import the practice backing
setup.separation.external.step2.body: Use your preferred off-vocal or karaoke backing. If you only have the original song, import the instrumental.wav generated by UVR5.

about.tagline: A desktop practice room — built for anyone who wants to sing, truly hear their own voice, and make every rehearsal audibly better
about.disclosure.title: Privacy and safety
about.disclosure.body: VocalSync Studio is local-first. Recording, pitch analysis, lyrics sync, and export run on your computer; network access is used only when you start YouTube download or tool installation.
about.notes.title: Getting Started
about.workflow.title: Recommended workflow
about.workflow.1: Import a backing track on the Setup tab, or download one from YouTube.
about.workflow.2: If you have the original song, separate vocals.wav first with UVR5 / Moises.
about.workflow.3: Import vocals.wav in Pitch Curve Source; the app creates the pitch curve and enables guide vocal monitoring.
about.workflow.4: Choose your microphone and headphones, then run latency calibration on first use.
about.workflow.5: On the Recording tab, balance backing, microphone, and guide vocal volume before recording.
about.workflow.6: Play back the take, then export a vocal or mix WAV.
about.guide.title: Step-by-step VocalSync guide
about.guide.prepare.title: Prepare the song
about.guide.prepare.body: Load an instrumental track, or download audio from YouTube. If you only have the original song, create instrumental.wav and vocals.wav in UVR5 first, then import them back into VocalSync.
about.guide.separate.title: Create the pitch curve
about.guide.separate.body: Apply the separated vocals.wav as the pitch curve source. VocalSync analyzes the vocal melody, shows a reference curve on the Recording page, and enables guide vocal monitoring.
about.guide.record.title: Record and calibrate
about.guide.record.body: Choose your microphone and headphones, then run latency calibration on first use. Before recording, balance backing, microphone, and guide vocal volume until the headphone monitor feels comfortable.
about.guide.review.title: Review and export
about.guide.review.body: After recording, play back the take and check timing, pitch, and volume. Export a vocal-only WAV or a mix WAV with backing plus your recording.
about.guide.model.title: UVR5 separation tips
about.guide.model.body: Model choice stays in UVR5. Start with a common MDX/UVR model to check how well the song separates. For a cleaner vocal reference, run a second separation pass in UVR5, then import the final vocals.wav into VocalSync.
about.notes.1.title: Prepare a backing track
about.notes.1.body: Load an off-vocal / instrumental file (MP3, WAV, M4A, etc.) or download it directly from YouTube. Avoid versions with the original vocal, which interferes with recording.
about.notes.2.title: Pitch curve source (optional)
about.notes.2.body: If you want a reference line on the pitch curve, you can provide one via:
about.notes.2.li1.after: to separate a clean vocals track from the original, then import it
about.notes.2.li2: Load a MIDI file as the melody reference
about.notes.3.title: Guide vocal monitoring
about.notes.3.body: After importing a clean vocals track, the Recording tab shows a guide vocal volume row. The guide is headphone monitoring only, helping you follow the melody while recording, and is not mixed into exported vocal / mix files.
about.notes.4.title: Latency calibration
about.notes.4.body: First-time users should run the latency calibration (bottom of the Setup page) so the recording timeline aligns precisely with the backing track. The value is saved automatically.
about.notes.5.title: Lyrics sync
about.notes.5.body: Supports LRC / SRT / VTT / TXT import, YouTube subtitles loaded as lyrics, a global delay slider, per-line sync editing, and LRC / SRT / ASS export.
